      "partial_result": "**Verdict: conditional GO for exactly one paired 17-update fit-only smoke.** Five defects in the gate text need fixing before it is frozen. None of them requires a new search. As a screen, F0 holds up; as evidence for a mechanism, it is weak. I made no edits and ran no jobs. The only thing I computed was the per-query hit counts from the receipt, whose SHA matches `0d6a2418\u20266df6`.\n\n## What F0 actually supports\n\n- **The effect is small.** Of the 512 queries, 8 were fixed by the centroid basis and 1 was broken when compared with native; against the sham it was 9 fixed and 1 broken. Exact sign tests give p \u2248 0.04 and p \u2248 0.02. That is fine as a licence to screen, but the lower bound rests on about 2 queries.\n- **The metric favours the treatment by construction.** Product-mean PCA-128 directly maximises the spread of the very prototypes the scorer classifies against, on the same fit products. Leaving the query out removes one image, not the product. F0 therefore cannot say anything about unseen-product gain, and the doc correctly says so. The 100-update TRAIN-held gate is the first measurement that means anything, so a smoke pass is worth mechanics only.\n- **The sham does not control centering.** `fit_centered_pca(means)` centres on the equally weighted product mean. The sham's shuffled groups have a mean close to the image mean, and native uses the image mean exactly. So F0's treatment changed both the basis and the centre, and the sham only controls the basis half.\n\n## Must-fix defects in `docs/inshop_centroid_pca_encoder_smoke_gate_2026-09-28.md`\n\n1. **Resolve the centre confound explicitly.** \"Preserve PCA centering\" is ambiguous, because the head bias `-(W \u03bc)` (`train_sop_siglip2_compact.py:231`), the classifier proxies (sums of `pca.apply` rows) and the bank values (`member_bank_initial_values`) all inherit `pca.mean`.\n   - Declare now that the treatment is the F0 object: the product-mean basis together with its product-weighted centre. Do not switch to image-mean centring after the fact.\n   - Record `\u2016\u03bc_prod \u2212 \u03bc_img\u2016` and `\u2016W(\u03bc_prod \u2212 \u03bc_img)\u2016` against the median projected row norm.\n   - Any later mechanism statement must say \"basis+centre\", not \"identity directions\".\n2. **Pin the native replay authority.** \"Original pinned native17 receipt\" gives no path or SHA. Name both, list the exact fields to be compared (per-step loss to what tolerance, the 17 batch pixel/input hashes, and the initial vision digest), and say whether replay must be bitwise or within a tolerance.\n3. **Specify the RNG contract.** `nn.Linear(...)` inside the initializer draws from the global torch RNG (kaiming reset) before it is overwritten, and the augmenting `ImageRows` loader (`train_inshop_siglip2_unseen_gallery.py:912`) seeds from global state later.\n   - The centroid path must build exactly one `nn.Linear`, same as native, and make no extra draws.\n   - It must not compute the native basis \"for comparison\" without `torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[])`, following the pattern at `:788`.\n   - The 17 equal input hashes act as the enforcement check. Say that a mismatch means KILL, not debugging.\n4. **Name the degenerate-product rule.** In-Shop runs with `allow_singletons=True`. Under equal weighting, a singleton product enters as a single raw image carrying its full view noise. The full-fit refit also differs from F0, because it now includes the 512 query images.\n   - Require `bincount(classes) > 0` for every product, as the probe already does, and record how many singleton products there are.\n   - If `fit_centered_pca`'s singular-gap or rank check raises on the refit, that is a KILL, not a tolerance change.\n5. **Fix the cost-gate window.** Over 17 serial updates, a 1.05\u00d7 median-wall threshold measures noise and warm-up, not the initializer, since per-step compute is identical by construction. Specify the step window (for example steps 2\u201317, matching whatever the native receipt used). Report initializer seconds separately from the step wall.\n\n## Minimal helper/API change and tests\n\n- **API:** add a strict keyword to `initialize_head_and_classifier`, `basis: str = \"image\"`, accepting only `{\"image\", \"product_mean\"}` and raising otherwise. Leave the default unchanged. The head, proxy and bank construction should stay untouched.\n- **Where the centroid code lives:** put the product-mean fit in the trainer module, computing the means with the probe's float32 `index_add_` and then passing them to `fit_centered_pca`. Do not import from the probe, and do not edit the probe, because its `source_sha256` is pinned in the receipt.\n- **Hash and checkpoint:** feed the basis name into the returned hash, so the two arms can never share a digest schema. Store the basis, mean and components in the checkpoint and receipt.\n- **Tests (one file):**\n  - The trainer helper equals the probe's `centroid_pca` exactly on synthetic data.\n  - `basis=\"image\"` output is bit-identical to the current output, which covers every existing caller.\n  - An unknown basis raises.\n  - One global RNG draw happens in both modes (compare `torch.get_rng_state()` after the call).\n- **Stale-default risk:** several diagnostics (`diagnose_sop_siglip2_fit_errors.py:262`, `probe_sop_siglip2_proxy_neighbor_coverage.py:111`) recompute the \"initial classifier\" with the default basis. They are outside this gate, but any later diagnosis of a centroid checkpoint must read the basis from the checkpoint. Otherwise it silently compares against the wrong init.\n\n## The rest of the gate is sound\n\n- Declaring the full-fit refit upfront, and not claiming it matches F0, is correct.\n- The frozen-lower-block, finiteness, variance \u226550% / rank \u226580% of its own initial value, and 32-image exact packed reload checks are all appropriate. Measuring against its own initial value matters here, because the centroid basis captures less total variance from the start.\n- The ban on any refit or shopping after a negative is right.\n\n## For the 100-update gate (next, not now)\n\nIt compares centroid against native with no sham. Given 433 \u2248 434 in F0, that is acceptable. It still needs two things frozen before it runs:\n\n- The held query/gallery construction.\n- Whether the native 100-update arm is a fresh paired run or a pinned exact replay.\n\nIts +0.5 pp mAP threshold with a product-bootstrap lower bound above 0 is the first quality test that counts, and it may well fail: after 100 updates with a trainable head, the difference in initial subspace could simply wash out.",
